newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle trading slows late in day - private.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle trading slows late in day - private.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trading slowed late Tuesday from moderate to active business in the morning at $66.00 per cwt, with a few at $67.00 in north Texas, feedlot sources said.
Some feedlot managers said this week's remaining cattle will be priced at $66.00. A few bids of $65.50 were passed in Texas.

At $66.00, cattle feeders said they would earn a small profit because of good rates of gain and cost of gains. They said no special conditions were attached to Tuesday's sales, with shipments expected within the normal seven days.

Some of Tuesday's sales should be shipped late this week, while others may go out early next week. It appears most of last week's sales have been shipped, with some loads scheduled for delivery early Wednesday.

USDA confirmed sales as of mid-afternoon Tuesday at 30,300 head in Kansas, bringing the week-to-date total there to 48,900 head. Sales in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area reached 29,600 head as of midday, bringing the weekly total there to 55,900 head, according to USDA.
